section.hint: Things I built because I wanted them to exist, hosted on my own subdomains. The interesting part is usually the constraint, not the interface.

items.name: XpenseSplitter
items.tagline: Shared expense tracking for group trips — no server, no accounts, and trips that travel by link.

image.alt: The XpenseSplitter landing screen, headed "Split the trip. Settle up in seconds."

items.why: Splitting costs on a trip always ends the same way: a spreadsheet nobody keeps up to date, or an app that wants everyone to make an account before it will accept a number. I wanted one where the maths is provably right and the data never leaves the people on the trip. So there is no server, no database and no sign-up — a trip is a file you can hand over, or a link that carries it.
features: Chronological ledger — amount, category, payment type, who paid, and who splits it.
A read-only explorer to search, sort and group; the ledger itself stays unsorted.
Settlement two ways: every pairwise debt, or the fewest transfers that clear everyone.
Merge another trip in from a saved trip or a file; the source is left untouched.
A trip shares as a link — no account, nothing uploaded, and nothing to expire.
Many trips side by side; switch, rename or delete, and an empty one is never saved.
notes: Largest-remainder rounding, so a split always sums back to the total.
Merging resolves identity first: the same person has a different id in each file.
The share link lives in the URL fragment, which browsers never send to a host.
A lineage id tells an arriving link which copy is newer, with no server to arbitrate.
Sentinels tell a clipped link from a mangled one; neither ever half-decodes a trip.
The zip is written with the browser's own CompressionStream — no dependency.
